headings.text: How it relates to the platform

blocks.html:
This page orients you on what the Matrix integration is and how it fits into the OpenDefence platform — read it before the runtime-architecture deep dive. It is for developers and operators; end users should head straight to the Matrix Guide book on the Guides shelf.

What Matrix does here

Matrix is the platform's secure messaging product: a Synapse homeserver per deployment, used by the unit through Element clients (desktop and mobile). Voice and video come from Element Call, backed by a bundled LiveKit SFU. On first login every user is auto-joined to a deployment space with general, helpdesk and offtopic rooms, so a fresh deployment is immediately usable.

One deliberate design choice matters more than any other: federation is disabled. Both shipped overlays set SYNAPSE_FEDERATION=off, so there is no server-to-server traffic with any other Matrix homeserver — each deployment is a closed messaging island for its unit. The homeserver.yaml mechanics and the entrypoint's other federation modes are on Matrix stack (Kubernetes).

The pieces

Everything runs in one pod (Deployment matrix, namespace app-matrix):

Piece Role
synapse-server The Matrix homeserver (Synapse), client API on :8008, delegating auth to MAS
mas Matrix Authentication Service — handles Matrix login as an OIDC client of the platform's Keycloak (realm RASENMAEHER); registers its own client in Keycloak on first boot
matrixrmapi The integration API on :8012 — speaks the rmapi product contract, provisions Matrix users, and publishes the product UI files
livekit + matrix-rtc LiveKit SFU for Element Call media, plus lk-jwt-service (:6080) minting the LiveKit access tokens
matrix-ui-nginx Serves the product UI at /ui/matrix and the .well-known/matrix/{server,client} discovery files

blocks.html:
How it relates to the platform

Matrix is a product integration like TAK and MediaMTX, not a standalone install. The core registers it as product matrix at http://matrix.app-matrix.svc.cluster.local:8012/, using the standard registry and identity-pinning wiring described in Integration pattern.

Users are never created in Matrix directly. Identity lives in the platform's Keycloak/LDAP (see Core services): a user enrolls through Deploy App, and Element login flows through MAS to that same Keycloak account via OIDC. One enrollment, every product.

Matrix is also the reference worked example for integration authors — if you are building your own product integration, follow it step by step in Worked example: Matrix rather than reverse-engineering the manifests.

Where to go next

  • Using Matrix as an end user — the Matrix Guide book on the Guides shelf covers setting up Element on desktop and mobile and day-to-day use.
  • Runtime architecture — containers, ingress hosts, databases and secrets are on Matrix stack (Kubernetes), which describes the closed-alpha pvarki/opendefence-platform.
